snapshot.name: elite_std.z80
snapshot.note: Start state of the "[a]" tape (`python -m nexclash.elite_std start elite_std_a.tap OUT.z80`: loads, types the Lenslok code from 0xC799, stops at the entry 0xD07F). 48K.

recordings.name: elite_std_a.tap
recordings.role: The "[a]" tape (49,068-byte block, Lenslok): the main snapshot is its start state (`python -m nexclash.elite_std start`, reproduces the .z80 byte for byte).

recordings.name: elite_std_jcv.tap
recordings.role: ELITEJCV / "[Joystick]" tape (42,242-byte block): rework jcv's start state (reproduces byte for byte).

recordings.name: elite_std_e128.tap
recordings.role: ELITE128, the original Firebird tape (scrambled block, layout B): rework e128's start state (reproduces byte for byte).

verify.note: No RZX of the standard game exists: lockstep from scripted states (nexclash/elite_std_verify.py): the build on a Next model against the original per instruction (PC, registers but I, RAM, port writes, bus-byte variations), title / docked / launch / flight / combat cases injected through the game's own dispatcher, 8 gap cases (equipment pokes: docking computer, escape pod, energy bomb, galactic hyperdrive, in-system jump, game over, an explosion, a missile hit; each must execute its proof routine), the title renders put back exactly (title_render_check); IM 2 unit cases with negative controls; boot check. Reworks jcv and e128 the same on their own start states.

status.title: Elite (standard Firebird release)
status.build: elite_std.nex: the original "[a]" game from its real start (title, Load New Commander), 3.5 MHz, mono, the IM 2 fix only, plus the title ship redrawn every frame (50 fps) at the original's angular speed; reworks jcv (Joystick tape) and e128 (the original Firebird tape, layout B)
status.software: auto: lockstep verify, every case of a / jcv / e128 (25 / 24 / 25, 8 gap cases each reaching its routine) exact against the original, title renders put back exactly, negative controls caught; boot check; CSpect: title, launch, flight all three
status.next: Hardware: title ship DMA / 28 MHz copy timing, loading screen, NXC on the card, the IM 2 fix

techniques.target: title screens only: per pass the game's own frame, then renders of the slot extrapolated from the last pass's change with the game's draw (A6DF / E008) and copy, the slot, work bytes and buffer put back
alt ROM image 1 = Sinclair's 48K ROM + the uniform IM 2 table and the hook entries in its free 0xFF area

pacing.coverage: Title loops of the three start states (simulator, 3.5 MHz) and a CSpect pass log; flight passes from scripted runs.
pacing.result: Title: 8.68 (jcv) / 10.90 (a) / 10.86 (e128) frames per pass; K = 8.27-8.29 lines at 3.5 MHz per 28 MHz line; flight at the original speed (no change).

dependencies.coverage: Access and writer survey of layout A in flight / docked / title; layout B writers over the 17 base cases (gaps/B/writers.json); the title draw's read and write sets (drawwrites.py, widened).
dependencies.result: The game runs unchanged; only the IM 2 vector (layout A) and the title loops' CALL sites are hooked; the draw reads only the slot and blueprint.

feasibility.decision: Owner 2026-11-23: the standard release is the baseline (original look), Lenslok skipped, three versions, the title ship smooth; the hack is an NXC option.
feasibility.next_experiment: Hardware: title renders at 50 fps with no tearing and the pass length within one frame of the original's over 100 passes.

results.check: lockstep verify from scripted states + title_render_check
results.scope: a 25 cases, jcv 24, e128 25 (2026-11-24, 8 gap cases each: docking computer to escape pod, game over, explosion, missile hit): every case exact, title renders (a 125, jcv 70, e128 120) put back exactly, negative controls caught.
